name: Doug Alexander
note: Alexander was vice president of Associated Students in 1970-71 under John Lyne. The 1971 Talisman caption lists the Executive Council as Brett Butler, treasurer; Carol Gray, secretary; John Lyne, president; Peggy Hundley; Joe Gerard; Glen Sweet; and Doug Alexander, vice president. The volume describes the Executive Council as the four executive officers plus three members elected from Congress.

name: Brett Butler
note: Butler was treasurer of Associated Students in 1970-71. He appears only in the Executive Council photograph caption; the yearbook's signed essay by Lyne does not discuss individual officers.

name: Carol Gray
note: Gray was secretary of Associated Students in 1970-71. As with Butler, the only appearance is the Executive Council photograph caption.

name: Reginald Glass
note: Glass was vice president of Associated Students in 1971-72 and the yearbook calls him the first black vice president of the body and the first black student to hold any high student leadership position at Western. As vice president he assisted the president, sat on the Academic Council as one of two voting student members, and chaired the activities committee. He was a member of Alpha Phi Alpha, which received its national charter on 31 October 1971, and was named outstanding Black Greek. The 1974 Talisman records a later chapter: as ASG representative from the Graduate College he resigned in protest, having asked for better minority representation in student government and on the Academic Council.

name: Nancy Pape
note: Pape was secretary of Associated Students in 1971-72 under Linda Jones. The volume notes the four A.S. officers attended conferences and meetings at national level during the year.

name: Joe Glasser
note: Glasser was treasurer of Associated Students in 1971-72. A Jack Glasser is separately listed as junior class treasurer in the same volume; the yearbook treats them as two names and this archive should not merge them.

name: Charles Boteler
note: Boteler was administrative vice president in 1972-73, the first year the office existed in that form. The volume explains that the revised constitution split the vice presidency in two, one for administrative duties and one for activities, and that Boteler and Mike Fiorella held them respectively.

name: Pat Newton
note: Newton was ASG treasurer in 1972-73. The same paragraph sets out the remade Congress: ten representatives at large, two from each academic college, the president and vice president of each class, and the ten Academic Council members and alternates.

name: Debby Clark
note: Clark was ASG secretary in 1972-73, the year the body took the name Associated Student Government in place of the Office of Associated Students.

name: Don Carter
note: Carter led the ten-member Judicial Council in 1972-73, which heard student appeals on parking tickets, dorm campusing and election violations and served as the deciding court for campus rule violations.

name: Glenn Jackson
note: Jackson was administrative vice president in 1973-74 and the yearbook's spokesman for the reorganization bill that abolished ASG's committee system and folded all programs into two areas, student affairs and academic affairs. He said the old system was too rigid and that ideas often fitted no committee, leaving some with nothing to do and others with too much. He also co-ordinated the free university, and cited lack of interest and difficulty finding teachers as its main problem.

name: Thomas LaCivita
note: LaCivita was activities vice president in 1973-74 and again in 1974-75, making him one of the few officers to serve two consecutive years in this decade. The 1974 volume says he was elected in one of the closest races and carries a Herald reviewer's criticism of the concert programme; the 1975 volume has President Jeff Consolo crediting him with a more diversified entertainment series on a $42,000 budget.

name: Pam Stewart
note: Stewart was ASG secretary in 1973-74. She appears in the section's officer list and in a caption of officers conducting a meeting with Yater, LaCivita, Jackson and Goodpaster.

name: Lee Goodpaster
note: Goodpaster was ASG treasurer in 1973-74 and appears in the same officer list and meeting caption. The yearbook mentions her separately in its elections and homecoming coverage.

name: Ricky Johnson
note: Johnson was ASG treasurer in 1974-75. The caption shows him discussing the signing of War and the Charlie Daniels Band with activities vice president Tom LaCivita. A Rickie Johnson appears on the ASG Congress attendance roll printed in the 1976 Talisman, so he may have stayed in Congress the following year; the spelling differs between the two volumes and is not settled.

name: Cindy Kirkpatrick
note: Kirkpatrick was ASG secretary in 1974-75, shown checking meeting notes while Consolo conferred with Panhellenic Council president Donna Filburn. She also appears in the 1974 Talisman talking with LaCivita and Vice President for Academic Affairs Dr. John Minton.

name: Marc Levy
note: Levy was an ASG Congress member in 1974-75 and again in 1975-76. In a letter to the College Heights Herald he wrote that he had hoped the year's meetings would differ from the previous year's invisible congress, and reported a good number absent from the 1 October 1974 meeting, at which three of four committee reports were given by the president himself. In 1975-76 he brought charges against ASG treasurer David Payne over spending before budget approval, appeared twice before the Judicial Council, and lost, the council ruling in Payne's favour.

name: Christy Vogt
note: Vogt was ASG administrative vice president in 1975-76. She ran the book exchange ASG co-sponsored with Veterans on Campus from 12 to 26 January 1976, reporting that the two groups had covered expenses by 21 January on sales of over 600 books at a margin of 25 cents a book. She said the executive officers were closer than in any past administration she had witnessed.

name: Rick Kelley
note: Kelley was ASG activities vice president in 1975-76. He introduced a bill in October creating a student activities committee, whose members were chosen in December from open applications and which ran three subcommittees for concerts, lectures and special events and publicity. The volume credits the year's concerts with turning a profit of around $4,300 for ASG. His surname is printed both Kelley and Kelly in the same volume; the spelling is not settled.

name: David Payne
note: Payne was ASG treasurer in 1975-76. Congress member Marc Levy brought charges against him for spending before budget approval had been given, and Levy appeared twice before the Judicial Council. Payne argued the constitution provided for such spending and the council ruled in his favour. Note for the editor: years.json carries a David Payne under 1982-83 as an unresolved name. These may or may not be the same person and this archive should not merge them without a source that links them.

name: Nancy Wilk
note: Wilk was ASG secretary in 1975-76 and kept the attendance roll the yearbook printed in full, effective 6 April 1976. She explained the rule: a warning after four absences and automatic removal from Congress after two more. The printed roll names some fifty Congress members and marks Mitchell Deep as resigned.
